expectations.name: 01-page-written
expectations.text: A runbook is written under docs/runbooks/, the kind the map gives what to do when a trigger fires.

expectations.name: 02-structure
expectations.text:
Each page the agent wrote or changed meets the map's structural rules: a declared kind, listed in its guide, links
and anchors that resolve, the kind's sections in order, a record named NNNN-<slug>.md, no rejected synonym.

expectations.name: 03-lead
expectations.text: The runbook opens with a lead under its title, not a restatement of the title.

expectations.name: 04-reason-told
expectations.text:
The runbook says why it exists, told as it happened: the worker stayed down after a deploy and receipts stopped
until someone who knew the fix was found, not only a conclusion such as "receipts can stop".
expectations.evidence: The intro tells the incident as it happened: "In the September 14 incident, the worker had stopped after a deploy; an earlier occurrence waited until noon because only Tomás knew the recovery steps." The title and audience line ("when members report missing receipt emails, especially after a deploy") tie this to receipts stopping. The cause, "the deploy script restarted only the web app", appears later under If it fails.

expectations.name: 05-fact-stated
expectations.text:
The run gives the query that counts the waiting jobs in procrastinate_jobs, on the runbook or in a script the runbook
names.
expectations.evidence: match /^\+.*procrastinate_jobs/ in ['diff']: {'diff': '+- `psql` access to the deployed `larder` database and permission to read `procrastinate_jobs'}

expectations.name: 06-trap
expectations.text: The runbook names a script: the map turns steps that are a fixed list of commands into a script the runbook names.
